answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a long chain of sequential modular squarings before it can produce a valid Wesolowski proof. The next squaring depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot shorten one clone’s delay by parallelizing that chain; they can run separate clones, but each incurs its own physical-time cost. Like a lantern marking an oasis through plume-filled air, the proof signals elapsed computation, not a unique person.
